title: Business card color family

location.series: Pentagram / Natural History Museum case study

slide_intent: Keep recognition stable while colors vary, because variation should not sever the connection between related materials.
strategic_value: A repeated purple ground and radial mark can allow different accent combinations to feel like one Museum identity.
demonstration: Scattered business cards pair purple symbol faces in several color combinations with a cyan contact-information face.
practical_value: Compare controlled changes to mark colors against a consistent base and layout.

content_islands.name: Symbol faces
content_islands.spec: Repeat the circular NHM mark on purple cards using different ring-color combinations.

content_islands.name: Contact face
content_islands.spec: Show one cyan reverse with name, museum name and small contact details.

content_islands.name: Arrangement
content_islands.spec: Scatter the cards at consistent diagonal angles to invite color comparison.

reference_purposes.Expression: Scattered business cards pair purple symbol faces in several color combinations with a cyan contact-information face.

ingredient.name: Ring-color combinations
ingredient.role: Provide variety while preserving one recognizable structure.
ingredient.application: Change ring colors against a repeated purple ground, as the business-card examples demonstrate.
ingredient.scope: Observed business-card family; these examples do not establish mandatory combinations or proportions.
